text: A rented ballroom, forty chairs, sixty journalists. {client} sits beside you, hands folded, media-trained and terrified. You tap the microphone once. The tone you choose now will echo through every question that follows.

reads.unreadable: Beside you, {client} wears the press smile. What is underneath does not reach the surface.
reads.likely: {client} is holding it together — barely, you think.
reads.clear: {client} is one wrong question away from the edge. Keep the wrong questions away.
reads.certain: You can feel it from your chair: {client} will follow your lead exactly as far as your lead deserves. No further.

choices.label: Humility — take the hit standing up
Counter-attack — call the story what it is
Disarm the room with a joke

text: "We are here because you have questions. Ask them." The room, braced for evasion, blinks. First question — a scalpel wrapped in courtesy.

choices.label: Answer it clean — honest, bounded, final

text: "Somebody is selling you a story, and the price is my client's name." A murmur. Attack buys attention — now you must be right, in public, on the record.

choices.label: Name the holes in the story, one by one
Pull back to the prepared statement

text: You open with the joke. Half the room laughs; the other half writes down that you joked. Everything depends on reading which half asks next.

choices.label: Read the room and pick the questioner yourself
Drop the act, read the statement

text: The first exchange lands your way, and the room's temperature drops a degree. Second round — the follow-up question, the one they actually came for.

choices.label: Take it head-on and close the book
Quit while ahead — closing statement now

text: The statement holds, but statements never end these rooms. Hands are still up. One more exchange, wanted or not.
A follow-up you did not see coming, a pause one beat too long — and the room smells blood. Pencils accelerate. This is the moment careers are written about.

choices.label: The spin doctor's exit — one impossible, perfect sentence
Find the one friendly face and give them the last question
Gather the papers and leave the podium

text: The closing line lands, flashbulbs pop, and for once they are on your side. Tomorrow's coverage will carry your framing in its first paragraph — which is the whole war, won.

effects.text: {client} faces the room — and the room blinks first
The press conference for {client} is a clean win. The story loses its teeth.

text: No knockout, no wounds. The story will run smaller, on a worse page, with your quote in it. In crisis arithmetic, that is a profit.

effects.text: {client}'s camp takes questions; the story shrinks a column
The press conference holds the line for {client}.

text: Twelve minutes, four questions, out. The room grumbles — but a short conference is a small target, and small targets survive.

effects.text: A short, safe press conference for {client}. Nothing gained, little lost.

text: Against every rule of media training, {client} speaks one unpolished, human sentence — and the room, which eats statements for breakfast, goes quiet. You could not have written it. That is exactly why it works.

effects.text: The sentence from {client} nobody at the press conference expected
One honest sentence from {client} does what no statement could.

text: You say the sentence — the one that concedes nothing, explains nothing and somehow satisfies everyone. Three papers will print it verbatim. Spin is a craft, and tonight the craft pays its rent.

effects.text: Quote of the week, courtesy of {agency}
The spin doctor's exit turns a stumble into the quote of the week.

text: The photograph of the empty podium runs everywhere, and empty podiums confess. Tomorrow the story is not the rumor — it is the conference. There is a way back from this, but it is uphill and it is long.

effects.text: Press conference implodes: the {client} story grows a second act
The press conference for {client} goes down in flames — and the room writes every flame down.
